candidate.answerReason: Each of the three corner triangles has \(3/16\) of the area of \(ACE\). Removing them leaves \(1-9/16=7/16\), agreeing with choice E.

methods.label: Compare and subtract the corner areas
methods.explanation:
The three triangles outside \(BDF\) are easier to compare with the whole triangle. Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\), and let \(S=[ACE]>0\). Triangles with bases on the same line and a common opposite vertex have the same altitude, so their area ratio equals their base ratio.

The given lengths show that
\[
\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac{CD}{CE}=\frac{EF}{EA}=\frac14.
\]
The remaining portions therefore satisfy
\[
\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{DE}{CE}=\frac{AF}{AE}=\frac34.
\]
For the corner at \(A\), compare areas in two steps:
\[
\frac{[ABF]}{[ACF]}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac14,
\qquad
\frac{[ACF]}{S}=\frac{AF}{AE}=\frac34.
\]
Thus \([ABF]/S=3/16\). Applying the same common-altitude reasoning at the other two corners gives
\[
\frac{[BCD]}{S}
=\frac{BC}{AC}\cdot\frac{CD}{CE}
=\frac34\cdot\frac14=\frac{3}{16},
\]
\[
\frac{[DEF]}{S}
=\frac{DE}{CE}\cdot\frac{EF}{EA}
=\frac34\cdot\frac14=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
The triangles \(ABF\), \(BCD\), \(DEF\), and \(BDF\) fill \(ACE\), with no overlap except along their boundaries. Consequently,
\[
\frac{[BDF]}{[ACE]}
=1-3\left(\frac{3}{16}\right)
=\boxed{\frac{7}{16}},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
